stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model handling practices.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI has released a batch of 722 manuscripts detailing solutions to various long-standing mathematical problems.
The breakthroughs stem from an unreleased frontier model, signaling advanced capabilities in complex problem-solving.
The announcement has generated significant discussion within the mathematical community regarding both the achievements and ethical implications of AI research.

stories.title: Mistral Large 4
stories.author: Philpax
bullet_points: Mistral AI has released a new large language model, Mistral Large 4.
This indicates continued advancement and iteration within the competitive LLM landscape.
The release is documented on the official Mistral AI documentation site.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard components in modern NLP/AI workflows.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags confirm its lineage within the transformer architecture and its connection to Meta's Llama family.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, serving a large community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Tesla’s Model 3 and Model Y can be a backup battery for your house
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Tesla is expanding its Powershare Home Backup feature to allow Model 3 and Model Y owners to use their EV batteries for home power during outages.
This functionality was previously limited to the Cybertruck and required the Powerwall 3.
The expansion now includes support for older Powerwall 2 and other Powerwall models.

stories.title: Google’s power-hungry data centers crave nuclear energy
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Google is partnering with Constellation to secure a 20-year power purchase agreement for nuclear energy.
The deal aims to supply electricity to Google's increasingly power-intensive data centers.
This move highlights the growing energy demands of major tech infrastructure and the push toward sustainable power sources.

stories.title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: OpenAI plans to implement default watermarking on ChatGPT outputs.
This feature is currently restricted to users within the European Union (EU).
The implementation is noted as not being perfectly reliable and being easily circumvented.

stories.title: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Hackers successfully obtained counterfeit TLS certificates for major services like Google.
The compromise originated from the breach of three domain registries.
This highlights a critical vulnerability in the infrastructure supporting digital trust and security.

stories.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: An open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
stories.author: ilreb
bullet_points: Introduction of EmbeddingGemma 2, a new open-source multimodal embedding model.
The model is highlighted as being lightweight, suggesting efficiency for deployment.
Its open nature makes it relevant for the broader AI/ML community and research.

stories.title: AnyPS5: Port PS5 binaries to PC without emulation (87% system libraries mapped)
stories.author: Fe2O3
bullet_points: A project named AnyPS5 aims to port PlayStation 5 binaries directly to PC.
The port achieves a high level of compatibility, with 87% of system libraries successfully mapped.
This represents a significant technical achievement in console emulation/compatibility layers.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings enhanced performance and broader model support.
Integration with GGUF models via llama.cpp expands compatibility across various hardware.
The update improves Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Xbox is reportedly securing exclusive streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI.
The news was teased by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma during an employee all-hands meeting.
This move suggests a significant strategic push by Microsoft into exclusive AAA gaming content.

stories.title: Apple and LG team up on new smart home gear, starting with a lock, doorbell, and thermostat
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple and LG are partnering to develop a new suite of smart home devices.
The initial products in the lineup include a video doorbell, thermostat, and indoor camera.
These devices will integrate with Apple's anticipated smart home hub, potentially launching around October 13th.

stories.title: HBO Max, Paramount+, and Discovery+ "will unify into a single service”
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Major streaming services (HBO Max, Paramount+, Discovery+) are reportedly planning a unification into a single service.
The consolidation is a significant industry shift in the competitive streaming landscape.
A potential consequence of this merger is the possibility of increased subscription prices for consumers.

stories.title: Partially Observable Zero-shot coordination by Predicting Intention of Partner
stories.author: Kuk-Jin Yoon
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of zero-shot coordination in embodied AI where partners are intermittently out of view.
Introduces 'Predicting Intention of Partner (PIP)' to handle ambiguous partner representations and hidden state uncertainty.
Utilizes a Joint-view VAE to synthesize richer partner representations from local observations alone.

stories.title: Beyond Waypoint Regression: Query-Based Cost Learning over Reachable Ego Futures for End-to-End Driving
stories.author: J. Marius Zöllner
bullet_points: The paper introduces a novel query-based cost-learning framework for end-to-end driving planning.
It addresses limitations of waypoint regression by estimating bounded costs for dynamically reachable ego trajectory queries.
The method utilizes compact joint scene tokens to capture coherent multimodal agent futures and incorporate contingency awareness.

stories.title: Exploiting Acoustic and Content-Oriented Speaker Verification Attacks Against Multilingual Voice Anonymization
stories.author: Xiaoxiao Miao
bullet_points: The research investigates speaker verification attacks against multilingual voice anonymization systems.
It explores whether both acoustic and content-oriented information can be exploited by attackers in multilingual settings.
The study addresses a gap in current research, which has primarily focused on English-language ASV systems.

stories.title: ChartBmkAgent: Harness-Governed Multi-Agent Construction of Chart QA Benchmarks from Sparse Error-Taxonomy Specifications
stories.author: Peilin Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the lag between rapid MLLM advancement and conventional benchmark development in AI.
Proposes 'ChartBmkAgent' to automate the construction of Chart QA benchmarks from sparse error specifications.
Aims to create an expressive, on-demand task format to probe coupled perception and reasoning capabilities in MLLMs.

stories.title: DSV-Mem: Evaluating Multimodal Memory in Professional Workflows for MLLM Agents
stories.author: Nishant Sankaran
bullet_points: The paper introduces DSV-Mem to evaluate multimodal memory in MLLM agents within professional workflows.
Current MLLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too heavily on informal, everyday interactions rather than complex professional tasks.
Professional scenarios require handling structured, information-heavy artifacts, which existing benchmarks fail to adequately test.

stories.title: When Tools Lie: Reliability of Mathematical Agents Under Corrupted Tool Feedback
stories.author: Gayathri Lihinikaduarachchi
bullet_points: Investigates the reliability of AI agents when external tools provide corrupted or false feedback.
Uses a controlled corruption framework to test agents' ability to detect and correct erroneous tool outputs.
Evaluates agent performance across 31 mathematical problems under varying levels of tool deception.

stories.title: Natural Language Questions as an Interface for Knowledge Graphs: QRAKEN Graph Distillation and Semantic Self-Healing
stories.author: Giovanni Colavizza
bullet_points: QRAKEN introduces a training-free, ontology-agnostic neurosymbolic pipeline for grounding LLM generation in empirical graph evidence.
It addresses a key limitation in Text-to-SPARQL by preventing LLMs from generating queries that misrepresent unfamiliar knowledge graph data models.
The system uses an offline distiller to create TTQL, a compact description of populated multi-hop patterns.

stories.title: Mu-DisCoCat: A Variational Pipeline for Compositional Generalization on Quantum Processors
stories.author: Mehrnoosh Sadrzadeh
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of compositional concept generalization (CoCoGen) in AI.
It proposes Mu-DisCoCat, a variational pipeline that maps Compositional Distributional Semantics (DisCoCat) onto Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs).
This quantum approach aims to overcome the scaling bottlenecks inherent in traditional tensor-based compositional models.

stories.title: Do LLMs Act on What They Know? From Partner Representations to Cooperative Actions
stories.author: Kuk-Jin Yoon
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) handle cooperation with unfamiliar partners, specifically regarding unknown communication conventions.
The study uses a Hanabi-derived environment, testing LLMs' ability to infer intent conventions using linear probes.
While probes successfully recover intent conventions better than target conventions, the LLMs' actual receiving decisions do not consistently align with the sender's established convention.

stories.title: Beyond Waypoint Regression: Query-Based Cost Learning over Reachable Ego Futures for End-to-End Driving
stories.author: J. Marius Zöllner
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in waypoint regression planners, which struggle to incorporate deployment-time safety constraints.
It introduces a novel query-based cost-learning framework to estimate bounded costs for dynamically reachable ego trajectory queries.
The method utilizes compact joint scene tokens to capture coherent multimodal agent futures, improving planning robustness.

stories.title: Enhancing Diffusion Language Models with Autoregressive Post-Training Weights
stories.author: Pascal Frossard
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where Diffusion Language Models (dLLMs), often initialized from Autoregressive (AR) models, fail to leverage the AR model's post-training ecosystem.
The paper proposes a method to enhance dLLMs by incorporating existing AR post-training weights after the diffusion conversion process.
This work aims to combine the advantages of dLLMs (flexible token-update orders, parallel decoding) with the benefits derived from AR model fine-tuning.

stories.title: Surviving the Router: Optimizing Skill Injections for Retrieval and Execution
stories.author: Sahar Abdelnabi
bullet_points: The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in AI agents that use modular, third-party 'skills' managed by skill routers.
Current security evaluations often overestimate attack success by assuming malicious skills are already selected for execution.
The research demonstrates that in realistic multi-skill environments, the retrieval competition significantly reduces the effectiveness of injected skills.

stories.title: Conversation Is a Two-Body Problem: Dyadic Evaluation of Full-Duplex Dialogue Models
stories.author: Se-Young Yun
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current evaluation methods for full-duplex dialogue models.
Full-duplex models allow simultaneous listening and speaking for more natural, low-latency voice interactions.
Current evaluations are often 'single-sided,' failing to properly assess the complex, two-body nature of real dialogue.

stories.title: Natural Language Questions as an Interface for Knowledge Graphs: QRAKEN Graph Distillation and Semantic Self-Healing
stories.author: Giovanni Colavizza
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of LLMs generating inaccurate queries when interacting with unfamiliar RDF knowledge graphs.
Introduces QRAKEN, a training-free, ontology-agnostic neurosymbolic pipeline for grounding generation in empirical graph evidence.
The system uses an offline distiller to create TTQL, a compact description of populated multi-hop patterns.

stories.title: SAGE: Semantic Anchor-Guided Evolution for Grounded Medical QA Data Synthesis
stories.author: Ming Gao
bullet_points: Addresses the critical bottleneck of limited, high-quality, expert-annotated data for clinical NLP tasks like Medical QA.
Introduces SAGE (Semantic Anchor-Guided Evolution), a novel method for synthesizing necessary training data.
Specifically targets challenges in resource-limited clinical settings, bypassing privacy and reliance on large external corpora.

stories.title: DirectSpeech2LLM: A Simple End-to-End Framework to Mitigate Prompt Overfitting in Speech-LLMs
stories.author: Rajiv Ratn Shah
bullet_points: Addresses prompt overfitting in Speech-LLMs, where models fail to generalize beyond ASR tasks.
Introduces DirectSpeech2LLM, an end-to-end framework designed to preserve LLM instruction-following on unseen speech tasks.
The framework utilizes distance-based CTC loss computed over the frozen LLM embedding matrix.

stories.title: POLAR: Ontology-Guided Risk Prevention for Tool-Calling LLM Agents
stories.author: Chanjun Park
bullet_points: Introduces POLAR, a new guardrail framework designed to prevent operational risks in LLM tool-calling agents.
Addresses the limitation of existing safety mechanisms which are often reactive rather than pre-emptive.
POLAR assesses action reversibility using a structured, auditable verdict, improving upon current fine-tuning or runtime check methods.

stories.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) where group-relative objectives lose signal when all rollouts receive the same reward.
Proposes 'Self-Retrospection Distillation' to allow agents to learn from past experiences to improve future anticipation.
Focuses on using hindsight to generate useful learning signals even when immediate scalar rewards are uniform across trajectories.

stories.title: Language Carries the Expert's Impression: Instrument-Anchored LLM Judges Transfer Counseling-Quality Assessment and Beat In-Domain Training
stories.author: Elisabeth André
bullet_points: Addresses the data scarcity bottleneck in automatically assessing communication quality in counseling conversations.
Presents a study demonstrating successful cross-domain transfer of expert impression prediction across different counseling corpora.
Findings suggest that training on external, related domains can outperform training solely on the target in-domain data.

stories.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
stories.author: Gautier Viaud
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in LLM agents: their lack of operational knowledge when facing new environments.
The proposed method, DAEDALUS, aims to bootstrap agent memory by leveraging self-generated tasks.
This approach seeks to reduce task failures and long execution trajectories without relying solely on pre-written human guidelines or extensive procedural training.

stories.title: Are Language Models Script-Aware?
stories.author: Fabio Rinaldi
bullet_points: The research investigates 'off-target generation,' where LLMs produce outputs in unintended languages or scripts.
It specifically addresses the understudied aspect of script knowledge, which is foundational before linguistic understanding.
The study tests Small and Large Language Models (SLMs/LLMs) on multi-scriptic languages to gauge their script awareness.

stories.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
stories.author: OfficialTurkey
bullet_points: OpenAI is sharing its progress and research related to Artificial Intelligence in mathematics.
The content is hosted on a dedicated GitHub repository, suggesting open access to technical work.
The focus on AI in mathematics indicates a push toward advanced capabilities in symbolic reasoning and problem-solving.

stories.title: The Witness Was the Suspect: Why AI Audit Logs Can't Be Trusted
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical vulnerability of AI audit logs, suggesting they may be untrustworthy.
It highlights scenarios where AI agents can cause significant operational errors, such as data leaks or database corruption.
This points to a growing industry concern regarding the reliability and accountability of autonomous AI systems.

stories.title: Claude Code Context Is Like a Fridge - Put Only Perishable Items in It
stories.author: iggredible
bullet_points: The article uses the 'fridge' analogy to explain the finite context window limitations of large language models like Claude.
It advises developers on context management strategies, distinguishing between main conversation threads and auxiliary processing.
Solutions proposed include utilizing subagents, separate sessions, or headless loops to manage complex, large-scale tasks.
